prompt: We are developing a new agent-learning method, and need one implementable operation, not more renamed concepts. Existing experiments: truthful misleading experience changes world-model predictions but strong ScienceWorld/DiscoveryWorld agents recover; task harm absent. Reactor Lab native tasks: granted affine family, target-only minimum decimal coefficient length solves 3/3, so consensus over all consistent models offers no advantage. OPINE program-model query memory is an ordinary missing branch-state isolation issue already anticipated upstream. Classical homing/synchronization is known. Other direct priors: active learning, bisimulation/successor fingerprints, causal retention/selective retesting, learned epistemic reach, policy-aware model losses, meta-learning adaptation, future-correctability/teachability. Do not rebrand these. We can run native DiscoveryWorld, ScienceWorld, ARC/OPINE or CausalGame cheaply; one RTX4090, no long training yet. Propose ONE concrete algorithmic operation that uses already collected true transitions differently than strong standard model learning, and predicts an actual task benefit. Specify exact inputs, computation/update, decision rule; identify the strongest existing algorithm it may reduce to and the precise non-equivalence or openly say no novelty if equivalent. Give a short falsification test on an actual named native task. Prefer a broad mechanism in one sentence but do not assert it is new without literature evidence. Keep under 700 words. Prior failed suggestion successor-fingerprint pooling was just state abstraction. We need implementable progress, not an audit plan.
